top_categories.workout_context: 74ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Granfondo Matildica's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before September.

Road-specific control matters at Granfondo Matildica. Practice on rolling hills: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 95 miles.
At Granfondo Matildica, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
7,054ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Granfondo Matildica. Train it until it feels boring.
At mile 60 of 95, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
7,054ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Granfondo Matildica. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on rolling hills can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 95 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,054ft of climbing on rolling hills does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.weather: September in Reggio Emilia, Emilia-Romagna, Italy — Mid-September in Reggio Emilia can still be warm, while the long route reaches higher Apennine roads where temperatures and rain exposure can change during the day. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking before Granfondo Matildica. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Granfondo Matildica’s 95 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Granfondo Matildica. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Granfondo Matildica rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on rolling hills to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Road Specific to prepare you for 95 miles of rolling hills in Reggio Emilia, Emilia-Romagna, Italy.
